cases.explain: Both nouns are the subject of «гремели», and a subject stands in the nominative — here the nominative plural кимвалы.

cases.sentence: И вот – влетел в мой ___, и пролетел вдоль вагона.
cases.explain: «В» answering «куда?» (motion into) takes the accusative; вагон is inanimate, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: Я ухватил ее сзади, она задыхалась от ___.
cases.explain: The preposition «от», giving the cause of something, always governs the genitive: от бега.

cases.sentence: Вернулась – и съездила меня по левой ___.
cases.explain: «По» meaning a blow landing on a surface takes the dative, so щека becomes щеке.

cases.sentence: Хор Эриний бежал обратно прямо на меня, паническим ___.
cases.explain: A bare instrumental with no preposition is used to say in what manner or in what guise someone moves — running 'as a panicked herd'.

cases.sentence: И где то счастье, о котором пишут в ___?
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) requires the prepositional — here the prepositional plural газетах.

cases.sentence: Обхватила мою голову и поцеловала меня в ___.
cases.explain: «В» marking the spot a kiss or blow lands on takes the accusative; лоб is inanimate, so the accusative matches the nominative.

reading.question: How does Venichka react when the Erinyes burst through his carriage?
reading.explain: His hair stands on end, and beside himself he jumps up and starts stamping his feet.

reading.question: What sound accompanies the Erinyes as they pour into the carriage?
reading.explain: Their pursuit is scored with thundering tambourines and cymbals, which are still clashing in the final paragraph.

reading.question: How do the goddesses of vengeance answer Venichka's shout that nobody in the world is guilty?
options: They ignore him and keep running
reading.correct: They ignore him and keep running
reading.explain: He begs them to stop, but they simply go on running past him.

reading.question: What does Venichka ask the last Erinys when he catches hold of her?
options: Where they are all running to
Whether the train stops at Petushki
reading.correct: Where they are all running to
reading.explain: He grabs her from behind and demands to know where they — and everyone — are going.

reading.ru: Съездила, взвилась к потолку и ринулась догонять подруг.
reading.question: What does the Erinys do immediately after striking Venichka?
options: Soars up to the ceiling and races after her companions
reading.correct: Soars up to the ceiling and races after her companions
reading.explain: She lands the blow, shoots up to the ceiling and rushes off to catch up with the others.

reading.ru: Я бросился следом за ней, преступно выгибая шею…
reading.question: What does Venichka do once she has flown off?
options: He throws himself after her, craning his neck
He goes back to his seat
He starts gnawing another sunflower seed
reading.correct: He throws himself after her, craning his neck
reading.explain: He rushes after her, bending his neck round — 'criminally', as he puts it — to keep her in sight.

reading.ru: Пламенел закат, и лошади вздрагивали, и где то счастье, о котором пишут в газетах?
reading.question: What question does Venichka ask himself amid the blazing sunset and the shuddering horses?
options: Where the happiness the newspapers write about is
When the train will reach Petushki
How much money he has left
reading.correct: Where the happiness the newspapers write about is
reading.explain: The blazing sunset and trembling horses prompt him to ask where the newspaper happiness has got to.

reading.ru: Вздымались вагоны – и снова проваливались, как одержимые одурью…
reading.question: How do the carriages behave as the Moscow–Petushki train goes off the rails?
options: They rear up and plunge down again, as if in a stupor
reading.correct: They rear up and plunge down again, as if in a stupor
reading.explain: Running through the train, he knows it is hurtling off the embankment while the carriages heave up and drop away again.

reading.ru: За ними следом гнался разъяренный Евтюшкин.
reading.question: Who is chasing the Erinyes when they come stampeding back down the train?
reading.explain: The tractor driver they were hunting at the start is now furiously driving them back the other way.

reading.ru: Вся эта лавина опрокинула меня и погребла под собой…
reading.question: What happens to Venichka when the stampede reaches him?
options: The avalanche knocks him over and buries him
He is thrown off the train
He is carried along on their shoulders
reading.correct: The avalanche knocks him over and buries him
reading.explain: He shouts for them to stop, and the whole avalanche of them flattens him and buries him underneath.

reading.question: Who is laughing in the chapter's closing line?
reading.explain: The chapter ends with cymbals still clashing, stars falling on the village soviet porch, and Sulamith laughing.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the man who came flying into Venichka's carriage?
sentences: …Двери вагонов защелкали, потом загудели, все громче и явственнее.
И вот – влетел в мой вагон, и пролетел вдоль вагона, с поголубевшим от страха лицом, тракторист Евтюшкин.
А спустя десяток мгновений тем же путем ворвались полчища Эриний и устремились следом за ним.
highlight.explain: Only the second sentence identifies the frightened runner as the tractor driver Yevtyushkin.

highlight.question: Which sentence says where the Erinys went after she had hit Venichka?
sentences: А покуда я грыз подсолнух, она отбежала немного, взглянула на меня, вернулась – и съездила меня по левой щеке.
Съездила, взвилась к потолку и ринулась догонять подруг.
Я бросился следом за ней, преступно выгибая шею…
highlight.explain: The second sentence is the one that follows the blow with her flight to the ceiling and after her companions.

highlight.question: Which sentence states what Venichka knew about the Moscow–Petushki train?
sentences: Пламенел закат, и лошади вздрагивали, и где то счастье, о котором пишут в газетах?
Я бежал и бежал, сквозь вихорь и мрак, срывая двери с петель, я знал, что поезд «Москва – Петушки» летит под откос.
Вздымались вагоны – и снова проваливались, как одержимые одурью…
И тогда я заметался и крикнул: – О-о-о-о-о!
highlight.explain: The second sentence contains the thing he knew — that the train was flying off the embankment.

highlight.question: Which sentence says who was pursuing the Erinyes on their way back?
sentences: Крикнул и оторопел: хор Эриний бежал обратно, со стороны головного вагона прямо на меня, паническим стадом.
За ними следом гнался разъяренный Евтюшкин.
Вся эта лавина опрокинула меня и погребла под собой…
highlight.explain: The middle sentence names the enraged Yevtyushkin as the one driving them back.
